# Preparation

## Load packages

```{r load-packages}
#| error: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| output: false
if (!requireNamespace("pacman", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("pacman")
pacman::p_load(
  tidyverse,
  janitor,
  MPTinR,
  afex,
  emmeans,
  RRreg,
  ggsignif, # for geom_signif()
  ggdist, # for stat_eye()
  ggtext,
  cowplot,
  knitr,
  kableExtra
)
```

## Import data

```{r import-data}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| output: false
dat_f <- read_csv("processed_data/s1_data_cleaned.csv") |>
  mutate(across(c(id, completed, condition, d_attention, gender), as.factor))
```

`dat_f` contains all participants who provided consent (*N*~consented~ = `{r} nrow(dat_f)`).

## Exclusion

```{r exclusion}
dat <- dat_f |> filter(d_attention == "Pass", completed == 1)
```

There were `{r} nrow(dat_f |> filter(completed != 1))` participants who did not complete the survey, and `{r} nrow(dat_f |> filter(d_attention != "Pass", completed == 1))` who completed the survey but failed the attention check embedded in D16. Excluding them leaves `{r} nrow(dat)` participants in the dataset for analysis.

# Analysis

## Sample demographics

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Age

```{r demographics-age}
sum(is.na(dat$age)) # The number of participants who did not answer
dat[dat$age < 18 | dat$age > 100, ]$age # Implausible values
dat |>
  filter(age <= 100 & age >= 18) |>
  summarise(m = mean(age), sd = sd(age)) |>
  kable(digits = 2) |>
  kable_minimal(full_width = FALSE)
```

### Gender

```{r demographics-gender}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
sum(is.na(dat$gender)) # The number of participants who did not answer
jmv::descriptives(dat, vars = "gender", freq = TRUE)$frequencies
```

:::

## Mind Game behaviors

### Descriptives

```{r mind-game-descriptives}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
# 1 = reported a match, 0 = did not report a match
dat |>
  filter(!is.na(match)) |>
  tabyl(condition, match) |>
  adorn_totals(where = c("row", "col")) |>
  adorn_percentages(denominator = "row") |>
  adorn_pct_formatting() |>
  adorn_ns(position = "front") |>
  kable(align = "r") |>
  kable_minimal(full_width = FALSE)

# Count data
mg_counts <- dat |>
  mutate(
    condition = factor(condition, levels = c("baseline", "cp", "norm")),
    match = factor(match, levels = c(1, 0))
  ) |>
  count(condition, match, .drop = FALSE)

get_mg_counts <- function(condition_name) {
  mg_counts |>
    filter(condition == condition_name) |>
    pull(n)
}
```

### Dishonesty by condition

We test whether there is evidence of dishonesty in each condition.

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Baseline

```{r baseline-dishonesty}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
DescTools::GTest(
  x = get_mg_counts("baseline"),
  p = c(0.2, 0.8),
  correct = "none"
)

effectsize::cohens_w(
  x = get_mg_counts("baseline"),
  p = c(0.2, 0.8),
  alternative = "two.sided"
)
```

#### CP

```{r cp-dishonesty}
)

effectsize::cohens_w(

```

### Multinomial processing tree models

#### Model specification

```{r mpt-model-specification}
mpt_model <- "
# Baseline tree
d1+(1-d1)*p
(1-d1)*(1-p)
# CP tree
d2+(1-d2)*p
(1-d2)*(1-p)
# Norm tree
d3+(1-d3)*p
(1-d3)*(1-p)
"
```

#### Saturated model

```{r mpt-saturated}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
mg_data <- mg_counts |> pull(n)

mpt_saturated <- fit.model(
  data = mg_data,
  model.filename = textConnection(mpt_model),
  list("p = 0.2"),
  output = "full",
  show.messages = FALSE
)

mpt_saturated$parameters |>
  kable(digits = 4, align = "r") |>
  kable_minimal(full_width = FALSE)
```

#### Omnibus test

```{r mpt-omnibus-test}
mpt_omnibus <- fit.mpt(
  data = mg_data,
  model.filename = textConnection(mpt_model),
  list("p = 0.2", "d1 = d2 = d3"),
  output = "full",
  show.messages = FALSE
)

mpt_omnibus$goodness.of.fit |>
  kable() |>
  kable_minimal(full_width = FALSE)
```

#### Condition comparison

::: {.panel-tabset}

##### Baseline vs. CP

```{r mpt-baseline-vs-cp}
mpt_baseline_vs_cp <- fit.mpt(
  data = mg_data,
  model.filename = textConnection(mpt_model),
  list("p = 0.2", "d1 = d2"),
  output = "full",
  show.messages = FALSE
)

mpt_baseline_vs_cp$goodness.of.fit |>
  kable() |>
  kable_minimal(full_width = FALSE)

# Effect size
dat_baseline_vs_cp <- dat |>
  filter(condition != "norm") |>
  mutate(condition = droplevels(condition))
effectsize::cohens_w(
  x = table(dat_baseline_vs_cp$match, dat_baseline_vs_cp$condition),
  alternative = "two.sided"
)
```

## Norms

### Descriptives

```{r norm-descriptives}
jmv::descriptives(data = dat, vars = vars(ee, pn, ne), splitBy = "condition")
```

```{r norm-descriptives-personal-normative-belief-frequency}
dat |>
  tabyl(pn, condition) |>
  adorn_totals(where = c("row")) |>
  adorn_percentages(denominator = "col") |>
  adorn_pct_formatting() |>
  adorn_ns(position = "front") |>
  kable(align = "r", caption = "Personal normative beliefs (count)") |>
  kable_minimal(full_width = FALSE) |>
  footnote(general = "1 = very inappropriate, 6 = very appropriate")
```

```{r norm-descriptives-normative-expectation-frequency}
dat |>
  tabyl(ne, condition) |>
  adorn_totals(where = c("row")) |>
  adorn_percentages(denominator = "col") |>
  adorn_pct_formatting() |>
  adorn_ns(position = "front") |>
  kable(align = "r", caption = "Normative expectations (count)") |>
  kable_minimal(full_width = FALSE) |>
  footnote(general = "1 = very socially inappropriate, 6 = very socially appropriate")
```

```{r norm-descriptives-different-norms}
dat |>
  summarise(perc = mean(pn != ne)) |>
  pull(perc)
```

### ANOVAs

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Empirical expectations

```{r anova-empirical-expectations}
#| message: false
mod_anova_ee <- aov_car(ee ~ condition + Error(id), data = dat)
nice(mod_anova_ee, es = "pes")
effectsize::eta_squared(mod_anova_ee, ci = 0.9, alternative = "two.sided")

emm_anova_ee <- emmeans(mod_anova_ee, ~ condition)
emm_anova_ee |>
  kable(digits = 2) |>
  kable_minimal(full_width = FALSE)
pairs(emm_anova_ee, adjust = "tukey")

# Cohen's d: CP - Norm (not model-based effect size)
effectsize::cohens_d(ee ~ condition, data = dat[dat$condition != "baseline", ])
# Cohen's d: Baseline - Norm (not model-based effect size)
effectsize::cohens_d(ee ~ condition, data = dat[dat$condition != "cp", ])
# Cohen's d: Baseline - CP (not model-based effect size)
effectsize::cohens_d(ee ~ condition, data = dat[dat$condition != "norm", ])

# Preregistered H5
contrast(emm_anova_ee, method = list(baseline_vs_cp_and_norm = c(1, -0.5, -0.5)))
effectsize::cohens_d(
  x = dat[dat$condition == "baseline", ]$ee,
  y = dat[dat$condition != "baseline", ]$ee
)
```

#### Personal normative beliefs

```{r anova-personal-normative-beliefs}
#| message: false
mod_anova_pn <- aov_car(pn ~ condition + Error(id), data = dat)
nice(mod_anova_pn, es = "pes")
effectsize::eta_squared(mod_anova_pn, ci = 0.9, alternative = "two.sided")

emm_anova_pn <- emmeans(mod_anova_pn, ~ condition)
emm_anova_pn |>
  kable(digits = 2) |>
  kable_minimal(full_width = FALSE)
pairs(emm_anova_pn, adjust = "tukey")

# Cohen's d: CP - Norm (not model-based effect size)
effectsize::cohens_d(pn ~ condition, data = dat[dat$condition != "baseline", ])
# Cohen's d: Baseline - Norm (not model-based effect size)
effectsize::cohens_d(pn ~ condition, data = dat[dat$condition != "cp", ])
# Cohen's d: Baseline - CP (not model-based effect size)
effectsize::cohens_d(pn ~ condition, data = dat[dat$condition != "norm", ])

# Preregistered H6
contrast(emm_anova_pn, method = list(baseline_vs_cp_and_norm = c(1, -0.5, -0.5)))
effectsize::cohens_d(
  x = dat[dat$condition == "baseline", ]$pn,
  y = dat[dat$condition != "baseline", ]$pn
)
```

We also conduct a Kruskal--Wallis test, as it may be more appropriate to treat personal normative belief as an ordinal variable given how it was measured.

```{r kruskal-wallis-personal-normative-beliefs}
kruskal.test(pn ~ condition, data = dat)
dunn.test::dunn.test(
  x = dat$pn,
  g = dat$condition,
  method = "bonferroni",
  altp = TRUE
)
```

#### Normative expectations

```{r anova-normative-expectations}
#| message: false
mod_anova_ne <- aov_car(ne ~ condition + Error(id), data = dat)
nice(mod_anova_ne, es = "pes")
effectsize::eta_squared(mod_anova_ne, ci = 0.9, alternative = "two.sided")

emm_anova_ne <- emmeans(mod_anova_ne, ~ condition)
emm_anova_ne |>
  kable(digits = 2) |>
  kable_minimal(full_width = FALSE)
pairs(emm_anova_ne, adjust = "tukey")

# Cohen's d: CP - Norm (not model-based effect size)
effectsize::cohens_d(ne ~ condition, data = dat[dat$condition != "baseline", ])
# Cohen's d: Baseline - Norm (not model-based effect size)
effectsize::cohens_d(ne ~ condition, data = dat[dat$condition != "cp", ])
# Cohen's d: Baseline - CP (not model-based effect size)
effectsize::cohens_d(ne ~ condition, data = dat[dat$condition != "norm", ])

# Preregistered H7
contrast(emm_anova_ne, method = list(baseline_vs_cp_and_norm = c(1, -0.5, -0.5)))
effectsize::cohens_d(
  x = dat[dat$condition == "baseline", ]$ne,
  y = dat[dat$condition != "baseline", ]$ne
)
```

We also conduct a Kruskal--Wallis test, as it may be more appropriate to treat normative expectation as an ordinal variable given how it was measured.

```{r kruskal-wallis-normative-expectations}
kruskal.test(ne ~ condition, data = dat)
dunn.test::dunn.test(
  x = dat$ne,
  g = dat$condition,
  method = "bonferroni",
  altp = TRUE
)
```

:::

## Predicting dishonesty

```{r logistic-regression-data}
dat_reg <- dat |>
  select(match, condition, ee, pn, ne, d_score) |>
  mutate(
    condition = relevel(condition, ref = "baseline"),
    ee_z = as.vector(scale(ee)),
    pn_z = as.vector(scale(pn)),
    ne_z = as.vector(scale(ne))
  )
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Model 1

```{r logistic-regression-model-1}
mod_1 <- RRreg::RRlog(
  match ~ condition,
  data = dat_reg,
  model = "FR",
  p = c(0, 0.2)
)
summary(mod_1)
```

### Model 2

```{r logistic-regression-model-2}
mod_2 <- RRreg::RRlog(
  match ~ condition + ee_z,
  data = dat_reg,
  model = "FR",
  p = c(0, 0.2)
)
summary(mod_2)
```

### Model 3

```{r logistic-regression-model-3}
mod_3 <- RRreg::RRlog(
  match ~ condition + pn_z,
  data = dat_reg,
  model = "FR",
  p = c(0, 0.2)
)
summary(mod_3)
```

### Model 4

```{r logistic-regression-model-4}
mod_4 <- RRreg::RRlog(
  match ~ condition + ne_z,
  data = dat_reg,
  model = "FR",
  p = c(0, 0.2)
)
summary(mod_4)
```

### Model 5

```{r logistic-regression-model-5}
mod_5 <- RRreg::RRlog(
  match ~ condition + ee_z + pn_z + ne_z,
  data = dat_reg,
  model = "FR",
  p = c(0, 0.2)
)
summary(mod_5)
```

### Model 6

```{r logistic-regression-model-6}
mod_6 <- RRreg::RRlog(
  match ~ condition * ee_z,
  data = dat_reg,
  model = "FR",
  p = c(0, 0.2)
)
summary(mod_6)
```

```{r logistic-regression-model-6-condition-specific-coefficient}
mod_6_coefficients <- RRreg::RRlog(
  match ~ 0 + condition + condition:ee_z,
  data = dat_reg,
  model = "FR",
  p = c(0, 0.2)
)
summary(mod_6_coefficients)
```

### Model 7

